Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays (particularly Figure 7) demonstrate marked tracheal dilation and multiple large, thin-walled intrapulmonary cavities/cystic changes, which are hallmark radiographic features of Mounier-Kuhn Syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly); management for this condition focuses on airway clearance and treating superimposed infections. *(guided by t000006)*
